era.title: The World Today
era.summary: Borders have barely moved since 2011. The changes are in names and flags, from Czechia and Eswatini to Türkiye and a new flag for Syria.

events.title: Malawi's rising sun returns
events.detail: Malawi brought back its original 1964 flag, with a red rising sun on the black band, two years after it was swapped for a flag with a full white sun.

events.title: Czechia as the short name
events.detail: The Czech Republic registered Czechia as its official short name with the United Nations. The full name, Czech Republic, is still in use.

events.title: Mauritania's new flag
events.detail: After a referendum, Mauritania added red bands to the top and bottom of its green flag, honouring those who gave their lives for independence.

events.title: Swaziland becomes Eswatini
events.detail: Marking 50 years of independence, King Mswati III renamed the country Eswatini, its name in the siSwati language.

events.title: Macedonia becomes North Macedonia
events.detail: The Prespa Agreement with Greece ended a long dispute over the name Macedonia. The country became the Republic of North Macedonia.

events.title: Turkey becomes Türkiye
events.detail: At Ankara's request, the United Nations began using Türkiye, the country's own name, in place of Turkey.

events.title: Kyrgyzstan's sun rays
events.detail: Kyrgyzstan redrew the sun on its flag with straight rays instead of wavy ones. The 40 rays and the yurt crown at its centre remain.

events.title: Syria's new flag
events.detail: After the fall of the Assad government in December 2024, Syria adopted the green, white and black independence flag with three red stars.

notes: assign is empty: every unit and piece is its modern self in 2026, using the app's world_flag assets (checked visually: AF tricolour, SY three-star flag, KG 2023 straight-ray flag, MR 2017 flag with red bands, MW 1964/2012 rising-sun flag). WorldCatalog already names CV Cabo Verde, CZ Czechia, SZ Eswatini, MK North Macedonia, TR Türkiye.

Modern target polities (CZ, MR, SZ, MK, TR, KG, SY, MW) are defined explicitly with asset flags so event 'to' chips resolve; they match the implicit unit-code polities and can be dropped if the merger resolves implicit ids.

Former-name/flag polity ids reuse exactly the ids and definitions the 2011 era assigns: SWAZILAND, MACEDONIA, TURKEY, CZECH_REPUBLIC, KG_1992, MR_1959, MW_2010, SY_1980. If the 2011 fragment renames them, update the 'from' lists here to match.

Malawi (2012 flag restoration) replaces Cabo Verde (2013, name only): 2011 assigns MW to MW_2010, so without this event Malawi's flag would change silently; Cabo Verde's flag never changed and 2011's CAPE_VERDE simply becomes CV.
Afghanistan: the Taliban's Islamic Emirate (2021) is not internationally recognised and the app keeps the tricolour, so AF is left implicit and no event is given.

Crimea (annexed by Russia 2014, unrecognised) is not a separate unit; left with UA. Somaliland (SO~somaliland), Northern Cyprus (XC), Kosovo (XK), Western Sahara (EH), Taiwan and Palestine are shown as the app shows them today.
Libya's 2011 flag change is an event of the 2011 era, so not repeated here.
Syria: flag adopted de facto in December 2024 and confirmed in the March 2025 constitutional declaration; year given as 2024.

Review (events/names/flags/copy): all four commons: flags exist, depict the pre-change flags, and are public domain. All event years, places and units check out; Cabo Verde (2013, name only) changes silently from 2011 CAPE_VERDE because the era is at the 8-event limit.
